main_text.p: singulari clementiâ, humanitate & facilitate, erga literatos inprimis, & ecclesiæ ministros, fretus pudorem illum & timorem tandem abstersi. Quâ ergo animi submissione & affectu Tuæ ego Celsitudini librum hunc humiliter ac demisse nuncupo, offero, dedico: eâdem ut clementiâ & benignitate illū accipiat, huicque meę audacię ignoscat, quâ possum & debeo animi subiectione & observantiâ oro. Pro accurato etiam suo judicio, vel addendo, vel auferendo, scriptū hoc Tuæ Cels. perpurget ac perpoliat. Quicquid enim Tuæ hîc arriserit Celsitudini, omnino rectum, utile & præclarum videbitur, atque erit omnibus.

Quod superest, Deum Opt. Max. omnis bonitatis fontem inexhaustum, & misericordiarum Patrem oro, ut conju-gium hoc, cum Illustris & Generosissimi Domini mei filiâ, Principe meâ clementissimâ, Cels. Tuæ diuturnū, jucundum, tranquillum & felix faxit; animâ & corpore utrique Cels. vestræ affatim benedicat; quæque penes Illustrissimam Cels. Tuâ deposuit animi bona & dotes, quoti-dianis incrementis ita adaugeat & locupletet, ut bonorum omnium & piorum,

Spelling is kept as printed: "illū", "diuturnū", "meę", "Tuæ", "Cels." is written Cels. (long s as plain s). The printed word "abstersi" is written "abstersi" and "deposuit" is written as printed in the scan. The left strip of text belongs to the facing page and was not transcribed.
